title: Practice Exam 9
description: An additional full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam. Challenging level.

questions.question: A traffic signal displays a steady red ball with a green right-turn arrow. You may:
choices: Make the right turn the arrow allows without stopping, yielding to pedestrians
Go straight because part of the signal is green
Do nothing until the red clears
Turn left on the arrow
questions.explanation: A green right arrow gives a protected right turn even though the ball is red—proceed without stopping but still yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk.

questions.question: You are stopped at a red light intending to go straight. The light turns green but pedestrians are still in the crosswalk ahead. You should:
choices: Wait for them to finish crossing before proceeding
Proceed; your green gives you priority
Creep forward to hurry them
Go around them
questions.explanation: Pedestrians lawfully in the crosswalk keep the right of way until they're across. Your green light does not let you drive into them.

questions.question: A signal shows a flashing red in all directions. Drivers should treat it as:
choices: A four-way stop
A four-way green
A yield for all
A signal to be ignored
questions.explanation: Flashing red in every direction means an all-way stop: each driver stops, then proceeds in turn when safe.

questions.question: A school bus is loading children at a stop on a multi-lane road and displays flashing red lights. Traffic in your direction (same side) must:
choices: Stop, regardless of how many lanes there are, until the red lights stop
Slow to 15 mph and pass in the far lane
Continue if in a lane not next to the bus
Stop only in the lane closest to the bus
questions.explanation: All lanes traveling in the same direction must stop for a school bus flashing red lights. Only a divided roadway exempts the opposite direction.

questions.question: You're driving 35 mph and enter a posted 25 mph school zone with children present. You should have:
choices: Begun slowing before the zone so you're at 25 or less upon entering
Braked hard right at the sign
Maintained 35 until you saw a child
Slowed only if a crossing guard was there
questions.explanation: Anticipate the reduced limit and slow before the zone, entering at or below the posted school-zone speed when children are present.

questions.question: A child on a bicycle wobbles along the edge of the road in a residential area. You should:
choices: Slow way down and give extra room; children on bikes are unpredictable
Pass closely at normal speed
Honk to make them move over
Expect them to ride in a straight line
questions.explanation: Young cyclists may swerve or stop suddenly. Reduce speed, allow plenty of space, and be ready to stop.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Watching for Children

questions.question: Two cars arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, side by side on perpendicular roads. The driver who must yield is:
choices: The one on the left, who yields to the driver on the right
The one on the right
The faster driver
Whoever is turning
questions.explanation: When two arrive together at a stop, the driver on the left yields to the one on the right.

questions.question: You're turning left at a green light with no arrow; an oncoming motorcycle is approaching. You should:
choices: Yield and wait—motorcycles are easy to misjudge for speed and distance
Turn quickly because a motorcycle is small
Assume the motorcycle will slow for you
Proceed because you have a green
questions.explanation: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic, and motorcycles' size makes their speed hard to judge—wait for a clearly safe gap.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Left Turns / Motorcycles

questions.question: Approaching a yield sign on a freeway on-ramp, you must:
choices: Slow or stop if needed and give the right of way to freeway traffic
Stop completely every time
Proceed without slowing
Expect freeway traffic to yield to you
questions.explanation: A yield sign means slow down, prepare to stop if necessary, and give the right of way—here, to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: Combining even a small amount of alcohol with a prescription sedative is dangerous because the two:
choices: Can multiply each other's effects, greatly increasing impairment
Cancel each other out
Have no combined effect
Only matter if you exceed 0.08%
questions.explanation: Alcohol and sedatives interact, intensifying drowsiness and impairment well beyond either alone. Don't drive after combining them.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Combining Alcohol and Drugs

questions.question: A driver's first DUI in California typically includes a license suspension of:
choices: At least several months, plus fines and a DUI program
No suspension for a first offense
A one-week suspension
Only a suspension if a crash occurred
questions.explanation: A first DUI brings a months-long suspension along with fines, a DUI program, and possible jail. Penalties grow with repeat offenses.

questions.question: You're in the left lane and want to move two lanes right to exit. With cars in the center lane, you should:
choices: Make one safe lane change at a time, signaling and checking each gap
Cross both lanes at once when there's a small opening
Slow down and force your way over
Wait until the gore point, then cut across
questions.explanation: Plan early and change lanes one at a time, fully completing each move. Don't cross multiple lanes in one motion or cut across at the last second.

questions.question: A broken white line on a freeway becomes a solid white line approaching an exit. The solid line means:
choices: You should not cross it; complete lane changes before it begins
You may cross it to exit
Traffic flows the other way
Parking is allowed
questions.explanation: A solid white line discourages or prohibits lane changes near exits and interchanges. Make your move while the line is still broken.

questions.question: On the freeway, the best general lane to travel in if you're not passing is:
choices: A right or center lane, keeping left lanes open for passing
The far-left lane at all times
Whatever lane has no cars, weaving as needed
The lane closest to on-ramps
questions.explanation: Cruise in a right or center lane and use the left lane mainly to pass. This keeps traffic flowing and reduces conflicts.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Choosing a Lane

questions.question: Your car starts to skid on a freeway curve in the rain. You should:
choices: Ease off the gas and steer smoothly in the direction you want to go
Brake hard and hold the wheel still
Accelerate to straighten out
Steer sharply opposite the skid
questions.explanation: In a skid, take your foot off the accelerator (avoid hard braking) and steer gently toward where you want the car to go until traction returns.

questions.question: Heavy crosswinds on an open freeway can push your car. You should:
choices: Slow down and keep a firm grip, ready to steer gently against the wind
Speed up to get through the windy stretch
Let go of the wheel to let the car settle
Drive in the far-left lane only
questions.explanation: Strong gusts—often near gaps, bridges, or passing trucks—can shove your car. Slow down, hold the wheel firmly, and make small corrections.

questions.question: Setting cruise control is unwise when:
choices: Roads are wet, icy, or slippery
On a clear, dry, open freeway
Traffic is light and steady
You want to maintain a constant legal speed
questions.explanation: Avoid cruise control on slick roads—it can make a skid or hydroplane worse and delay your reaction. Use it only on dry, open roads.

questions.question: You glance at a roadside billboard and drift toward the next lane. This shows that:
choices: Even visual distractions outside the car can cause lane drift—keep your eyes scanning the road
Billboards have no effect on driving
Drifting is unavoidable on the freeway
You should follow the car ahead more closely
questions.explanation: Where your eyes go, the car tends to follow. Avoid fixating on billboards, crashes, or scenery; keep scanning your path and surroundings.

questions.question: It is illegal for an adult to hold and use a phone while driving, but legal to:
choices: Use it hands-free, mounted, with a single tap or voice command
Hold it on speaker in your lap
Text at red lights
Watch navigation video while moving
questions.explanation: Adults may use a phone only hands-free—mounted and operated by one tap/swipe or voice. Holding it or interacting beyond a single touch is illegal.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Cell Phone Laws

questions.question: On a road posted 45 mph at night with light fog, an appropriate speed is likely:
choices: Below 45, slow enough to stop within the range of your headlights
Exactly 45, the posted limit
Above 45 to get through the fog faster
45 with high beams on
questions.explanation: Night and fog both shorten how far you can see. Slow below the posted limit so you can stop within your visible distance, and use low beams in fog.

questions.question: The speed limit at an intersection where you cannot see at least 100 feet in each direction (a blind intersection) is:
choices: 15 mph
25 mph
20 mph
10 mph
questions.explanation: Blind intersections carry a 15 mph limit for the last 100 feet before crossing—the same as alleys and unguarded rail crossings.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — 15 mph Speed Limits

questions.question: Driving the posted 65 mph in stop-and-go freeway traffic that's actually moving at 20 would be:
choices: Impossible and unsafe—you must match the safe speed of traffic
Your legal right regardless of traffic
Required to keep your place
Fine in the left lane only
questions.explanation: The posted number is a maximum; you must drive no faster than is safe for traffic and conditions. In congestion that means matching the slow flow.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Basic Speed Law

questions.question: A pedestrian is jogging across the street mid-block, against traffic. As a driver you:
choices: Must still slow or stop to avoid hitting them
May proceed since they're jaywalking
Should speed past behind them
Have no responsibility to avoid them
questions.explanation: Right of way is given, not taken. You must take reasonable action to avoid any pedestrian, even one crossing unlawfully.

questions.question: A bicyclist signals a right turn by holding the left arm bent upward (forearm up). You should:
choices: Expect them to move right and give them room to complete the turn
Expect them to turn left
Assume they're stopping
Pass them on the right immediately
questions.explanation: A left arm bent upward signals a right turn (an alternative to extending the right arm). Anticipate the cyclist's move and give space.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Bicycle Hand Signals

questions.question: When you pass a bicyclist and then need to turn right just ahead, you should:
choices: Not cut back in front to turn until you're well clear of the cyclist
Turn right immediately after passing
Slow in front of the cyclist to force them to stop
Pass and turn in one continuous motion
questions.explanation: Cutting right immediately after passing can trap a cyclist ('right hook'). Make sure you're well ahead, or merge into the bike lane near the corner to turn.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: You park on a steep hill facing uphill with a curb. The correct front-wheel position is:
choices: Turned away from the curb
Turned toward the curb
Straight ahead
Turned toward the center of the road
questions.explanation: Uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so a backward roll catches the tire on the curb. Set the parking brake too.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on Hills

questions.question: A yellow curb permits you to:
choices: Stop briefly to load or unload passengers or freight, within the time limit
Park overnight
Park only with a disabled placard
Stop for as long as you wish
questions.explanation: Yellow = loading zone. Stop only long enough to load/unload within the posted time. Some require you to stay with the vehicle.

questions.question: You want to park facing downhill with no curb. Set the front wheels:
choices: Pointed toward the edge of the road
Pointed toward the center of the road
Straight ahead
Pointed away from the edge
questions.explanation: No curb (uphill or downhill): point the wheels toward the road's edge so a runaway car leaves the roadway. Always set the parking brake.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Parking on Hills

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with siren is approaching you head-on in oncoming lanes on an undivided road. You should:
choices: Pull to the right and stop until it passes
Continue, since it's in the other lanes
Pull left to give it room
Speed up to pass it quickly
questions.explanation: On an undivided road, pull right and stop for an approaching emergency vehicle, even one in the oncoming lanes—it may need to cross or pass.

questions.question: After an emergency vehicle passes you, you should:
choices: Wait until it's well ahead, then merge back, staying at least 300 feet behind
Pull out immediately right behind it
Follow closely to use the cleared path
Speed up to keep pace with it
questions.explanation: Don't pull out right behind an emergency vehicle, and never follow within 300 feet of one running its siren or lights.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: A white regulatory sign reads 'LEFT LANE MUST TURN LEFT.' If you're in the left lane and don't want to turn, you:
choices: Should have moved right earlier; you must now turn left
May go straight anyway
May stop and wait to merge right
May turn right instead
questions.explanation: A mandatory-turn sign requires the lane to turn as directed. If you didn't move over in time, you must complete the turn and find another route.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Lane Use Control Signs

questions.question: A diamond-shaped yellow sign with a deer symbol means:
choices: Watch for animals that may cross the road, especially at dawn and dusk
A zoo is ahead
Hunting is allowed
A scenic area is ahead
questions.explanation: An animal-crossing warning sign means wildlife may enter the road. Slow down and scan the roadsides, particularly around dawn and dusk.

questions.question: A green guide sign on the freeway typically shows:
choices: Directions, distances, and exit information
A regulation you must obey
A construction warning
Available roadside services
questions.explanation: Green signs give guidance—route directions, distances, and exits. White signs are regulatory; orange signs warn of construction; blue signs list services.

questions.question: On a slick road, you should set your following distance to:
choices: More than 3 seconds, since stopping takes longer
Exactly 3 seconds, as always
Less than 3 seconds to stay with traffic
Two car lengths regardless of speed
questions.explanation: Slick surfaces lengthen stopping distance, so increase your following distance to 4 seconds or more.

questions.question: A motorcycle ahead of you is entitled to the full width of its lane. You should:
choices: Not share the lane or crowd it; give the motorcycle the whole lane
Drive beside it in the same lane
Pass within the same lane
Tailgate to save space
questions.explanation: A motorcycle has the right to the entire lane. Never share or crowd its lane, and give it a full following distance.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Motorcycles

questions.question: A traffic signal's left-turn arrow turns from green to yellow. This means:
choices: The protected turn is ending; finish only if you safely can, then it becomes unprotected or red
You have more time to turn
You must turn faster
Oncoming traffic is now stopped
questions.explanation: A yellow left arrow warns the protected turn is ending. Complete the turn if you're committed and can do so safely; otherwise stop and wait.
